t:
The Act of March 14, 1978 (92 Stat. 154), is amended as follows:

    (a) In section 1(a), in the first sentence, delete the phrase “two-year”, and change “September 30, 1980” to “September 30, 1985”; and 
    (b) In section 1(c) strike the second sentence in its entirety and insert the following: “There is authorized to be appropriated an amount not to exceed $1,500,000 annually for fiscal years 1979 through 1982 to carry out the provisions of this Act: Provided, That any appropriations made pursuant to this Act shall be reduced by the amount of any payments made to said districts pursuant to the Acts of September 23, 1950 (64 Stat. 906), as amended (20 U.S.C. 631 et seq.), and September 30, 1950 (64 Stat. 1100), as amended (20 U.S.C. 236 et seq.). For the authorizations made in this subsection, any amounts authorized but not appropriated in any fiscal year shall remain available for appropriation in succeeding fiscal years.”.

fable.w: This section only extends a statutory date and authorizes appropriations, with an offset for payments made to school districts under other Acts. The tempting reading is that the reference to payments to "said districts" (non-federal entities) signals outside involvement, but receiving funds is not consulting on or contesting a federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking, or right to sue appears.
fable.s: There is authorized to be appropriated an amount not to exceed $1,500,000 annually for fiscal years 1979 through 1982 to carry out the provisions of this Act

qwen_block.w: This section solely concerns the authorization of federal appropriations and the adjustment of fiscal dates. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The text describes internal budgetary authority rather than public participation.
qwen_block.s: There is authorized to be appropriated an amount not to exceed $1,500,000 annually for fiscal years 1979 through 1982 to carry out the provisions of this Act

opus.w: This amendment only extends a date and sets how much money Congress may appropriate, with reductions for other payments made to the districts. The mention of local school districts might look like outside involvement, but they are only receiving funds, and grants or benefits do not count as participation. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: There is authorized to be appropriated an amount not to exceed $1,500,000 annually for fiscal years 1979 through 1982 to carry out the provisions of this Act
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** It's tempting to read this as participation because it mentions payments to outside parties ("said districts", meaning local school districts). But those payments are federal funding, and grants and benefits are excluded under the definition. The section only changes a deadline and an amount of money Congress may appropriate. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, asked for comment or given a right to sue over a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends an act to change authorization levels and dates for appropriations. It mentions payments to districts but does not require any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in federal decision-making. The text is strictly about budgetary authorizations and statutory dates.
qwen_chat.s: There is authorized to be appropriated an amount not to exceed $1,500,000 annually for fiscal years 1979 through 1982 to carry out the provisions of this Act: Provided, That any appropriations made pursuant to this Act shall be reduced by the amount of any payments made to said districts pursuant to the Acts of September 23, 1950 (64 Stat. 906), as amended (20 U.S.C. 631 et seq.), and September 30, 1950 (64 Stat. 1100), as amended (20 U.S.C. 236 et seq.).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "districts" receiving payments implies some form of consultation or participation by those districts. However, the text only describes the funding mechanism and the reduction of appropriations based on other payments; it does not require the districts to consult with the federal government or participate in a decision-making process. The text is purely about appropriations and statutory amendments regarding funding levels.
